samples.summary: The frontend reader's new nesting cap has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff adds the identical depth cap to `treeNodeToBlock`/`treeNodeToRow`/`treeNodeToCell` in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` (the reader actually used in production), but only the docs-engine twin is tested (`packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts` exercises `src/model/crdt-tree.ts`). `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` has a whole band-clamping section (MAX_FONT_SIZE, MAX_CELL_PADDING, MAX_ROW_HEIGHT, MAX_LIST_LEVEL at lines ~3557-3641) yet no mention of MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH or deep nesting; grepping the whole frontend package for `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` matches only the source file. So a wrong or missing cap in the copy that every user's tab runs (depth not threaded through a branch, off-by-one, header/footer index-as-depth) would ship green — the exact stack-overflow-on-first-read DoS this change exists to close.

samples.summary: New dual-entry module `model/table-nesting.js` not added to the entry-parity allowlist
samples.evidence: `src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts` both gain `export { MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH } from './model/table-nesting.js'`, and node.ts's own comment records that omitting it previously broke at runtime with "does not provide an export named 'MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH'". The parity guard that exists precisely for this (`entry-parity.test.ts` it.each list: block-helpers, model constants, list-level, row-height, numeric-attrs) was not extended with `./model/table-nesting.js`, so the next export added to that module can drift between entries undetected — the failure mode the test file's header describes for `normalizeListLevel`.

samples.summary: Layout cap test only asserts "does not throw"; the truncation shape it documents is unasserted
samples.evidence: `test('lays out a chain deep enough to overflow the stack')` asserts only `not.toThrow()`. Nothing checks the invariant the implementation comment in `table-layout.ts` calls load-bearing: past the cap the nested table must lay out as exactly one empty line so the cell's `lines`/`blockBoundaries` stay in step with its blocks ("every caret and hit-test index depends on that correspondence"). A cap that `continue`d without pushing a line, or pushed two, would still not throw and this test would stay green while carets/hit-tests inside deep cells desynchronise. There is also no layout-side equivalent of the reader's "truncated at exactly MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH" assertion.

samples.summary: Cycle/clamp regression tests would hang the worker rather than fail, contrary to their own comment
samples.evidence: The comment at lines 327-333 claims "vitest's per-test timeout is what turns that into a failure rather than a wedged suite". The pre-fix behaviour in every one of these cases (`normalizeRange`'s `while` walk, `resolveNestedTableLayout`, `resolvePositionPixel`, and the `-1e9..1e9` clamp test whose `expandCellRangeForMerges` loops synchronously) is a *synchronous* infinite loop, which blocks the event loop so vitest's timer-based timeout cannot fire. If any of these guards regresses, CI wedges (or is killed by an outer job timeout) instead of reporting a failing test, which makes the regression signal much weaker than the comment asserts.

samples.summary: New cycle guards in `findOuterCellAddress` and `findOutermostTableId` are untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds `seen` sets to `TextEditor.findOuterCellAddress` (line ~3902) and the new `TextEditor.findOutermostTableId` (~3934). The cyclic-map suite in `nested-table-cell-range.test.ts` covers `resolveNestedTableLayout`, `normalizeRange`, `resolvePositionPixel` and `Doc.findBlock`, but nothing drives a TextEditor pointer gesture against a cyclic `blockParentMap`, so these two guards could be removed or mis-ordered (e.g. adding to `seen` after the return) without any test noticing — the hang would only surface for a user dragging in a document a peer poisoned.

samples.summary: `buildCellRangeRects` clamping and the unresolved-table branch of `normalizeCellRange` are untested
samples.evidence: The only clamp test ('clamps a peer-written cell rectangle to the table it names') goes through `normalizeCellRange` with a resolvable 2x2 table. Untested: (a) the new `rowStart/rowEnd/colStart/colEnd` clamp in `buildCellRangeRects` (selection.ts 724-728), which is the backstop for a rectangle whose table resolves in the layout but not in `normalizeCellRange`; (b) `normalizeCellRange` when `table` is undefined, where `maxRow`/`maxCol` are `Infinity` and a `1e9` index passes through unclamped; (c) the deliberately folded `maxCol` reduce (chosen over `Math.max(...)` to avoid RangeError past ~100k rows) — the fixture has 2 rows, so spread vs reduce is indistinguishable here.

samples.summary: No test covers the header/footer `.map(c => treeNodeToBlock(c))` wrapping (index-as-depth hazard)
samples.evidence: Both readers changed `blocks.map(treeNodeToBlock)` to a wrapped callback precisely because `map` passes the element index as the new `depth` argument — a header/footer whose 33rd+ block is a table would otherwise be read with all rows dropped. Grepping `docsTreeToDocument` across the repo matches only `src/model/crdt-tree.ts`, `src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts` — no test file — and the new suite exercises `treeNodeToBlock` directly, never the header/footer path. The same hazard in `treeToDocument` in yorkie-doc-store.ts is likewise unasserted, so re-introducing the bare `.map(treeNodeToBlock)` would ship green.

samples.summary: Merged-row shift+click test asserts only a rectangle count, not geometry
samples.evidence: `it('shift+click across the merged row covers the merge whole')` asserts `expect(rects).toHaveLength(5)` and nothing about where those five rects are or how wide the merged band is — five wrongly-placed or wrongly-sized rects pass. The sibling suite `table-drag-merge-selection.test.ts` decodes rects to `row,col` addresses via `cellsOf`/`calibrate`; that same decoding is not applied here even though the file already collects per-cell points.

samples.summary: Wafflebase-flavour clipboard assertion checks only row count, not cell contents
samples.evidence: `expect(payload.tableCells).toHaveLength(3)` is the whole assertion on the `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` payload produced by the newly nested-aware `getSelectedTableCells`; any three rows of any cells (wrong columns, wrong table) satisfy it. The fixture already puts `r{r}c{c}` text in each cell, so the payload could be asserted cell-by-cell the way the `text/plain` flavour is on the next lines.

samples.summary: `cellsOf` snaps any rect to a nearest grid address, so off-table rects can still read as valid cells
samples.evidence: `nearest()` reduces to the closest calibrated column/row origin with no tolerance, so a highlight painted far outside the table (or at a wrong page offset) is still reported as some `row,col` and can satisfy the `toEqual(ROWS_0_TO_2)` assertions. A distance bound (or asserting the raw rect against the calibrated x/y within an epsilon) would make the read-back non-vacuous for grossly misplaced paints.

finding.summary: The frontend reader's new nesting cap has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff adds the identical depth cap to `treeNodeToBlock`/`treeNodeToRow`/`treeNodeToCell` in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` (the reader actually used in production), but only the docs-engine twin is tested (`packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts` exercises `src/model/crdt-tree.ts`). `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` has a whole band-clamping section (MAX_FONT_SIZE, MAX_CELL_PADDING, MAX_ROW_HEIGHT, MAX_LIST_LEVEL at lines ~3557-3641) yet no mention of MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH or deep nesting; grepping the whole frontend package for `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` matches only the source file. So a wrong or missing cap in the copy that every user's tab runs (depth not threaded through a branch, off-by-one, header/footer index-as-depth) would ship green — the exact stack-overflow-on-first-read DoS this change exists to close.

verdict.reason: The frontend reader implements its own copy of the nesting cap (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:436-484, with depth threaded through treeNodeToRow/treeNodeToCell and reset in the header/footer wrappers at :558/:564), and I could find no test anywhere that exercises it. The only nesting test, packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts, imports treeNodeToBlock from packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.js — the engine twin, not the frontend store. Repo-wide greps for MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH and case-insensitive 'nesting' produce no frontend test hit; depth/deep/cap/overflow in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs only match the unrelated 50-entry undo cap. I also chased indirect routes: colocated packages/frontend/src/app/docs tests, the read-only and concurrent integration suites, tests/helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts, and packages/docs/test/store/entry-parity.test.ts (which only asserts export-name parity between the browser and Node entries, not cap behavior). Meanwhile the same frontend suite does cover this reader's sibling guards (MAX_FONT_SIZE/MAX_ROW_HEIGHT/MAX_LIST_LEVEL at yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3557-3641), so the nesting cap is the lone untested one. A lost depth argument in one branch or an off-by-one in the production reader would ship undetected, silently restoring the stack-overflow-on-first-read failure the guard exists to prevent — a major test-adequacy gap.
